- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) and forecast is rising sharply, reduce forecast peak by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.3) and forecast is falling, avoid under-shooting; slightly increase downward slope to align with mean reversion.  
- For 30-day horizons, if recent 5–7 day price action shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 2–3 consecutive days moving toward 70–75 range), adjust forecast to reflect tighter consolidation.  
- If sentiment spikes after a low, model tends to overreact — dampen forecast rise by 5–10% in next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment is neutral (0.3–0.7) and price is trending, avoid overfitting to recent volatility — use 3–5 day moving average as baseline for correction.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome deviates >10% from 14-day moving average of history, re-weight forecast toward historical mean unless sentiment strongly contradicts.  
- If sentiment is consistently positive over 3–5 days and price is rising, forecast should not exceed 1.2x recent 14-day high unless sentiment is >0.85.  
- If sentiment is negative and price is falling, avoid predicting below 10% below recent low — use 10–15% buffer to prevent premature bottoming.
